Visual Basic 6.0 (TStore.vbp) & VB.NET Source Code Inspector

Browse the complete, unmodified source code of RaggieSoft StoreTrainer authored between 2018 and 2020 inside a Windows 2000 Professional SP4 virtual machine. All source code is released under the MIT License.

Source File Index (16 Modules & Forms)

  • TStore.vbp — Master Visual Basic 6.0 project file defining forms, Win32 API modules, version metadata (v1.0.0), and compilation flags.
  • frmMain.frm — Main application form managing the PC game & trainer profile selector, command-line switch fields, and process launch triggers.
  • TStore.bas — Core Visual Basic 6.0 module orchestrating initialization, profile loading, and Win32 execution flow.
  • SFile.bas — Win32 file management and shell operations module for locating, copying, and launching game and trainer binaries.
  • INIFile.bas — Direct Win32 `GetPrivateProfileString` / `WritePrivateProfileString` (`kernel32.dll`) bindings for zero-database INI configuration persistence.
  • Registry.bas — Direct Win32 `RegOpenKeyEx` / `RegQueryValueEx` (`advapi32.dll`) bindings for reading game installation paths across 32-bit and 64-bit Windows.
  • SpecialFolder.bas — Resolves `AppData`, `Program Files`, and user profile directories across Windows 95 through Windows 11.
  • OSVersionInfo.bas — Queries `GetVersionExA` (`OSVERSIONINFO`) to detect Windows 9x vs. Windows NT kernels at runtime.
  • DetectOSBits.bas — Dynamically probes `IsWow64Process` in `kernel32.dll` so 32-bit `TStore.exe` knows whether it is running on a 64-bit Windows OS.
  • VersionCompare.bas — Uses `version.dll` (`GetFileVersionInfoA`) to inspect and compare executable version headers.
  • wHwnd.bas — Win32 `user32.dll` window handle (`HWND`) enumeration and process state tracking for launched games and trainers.
  • README.txt — Original plaintext user documentation bundled with StoreTrainer.
  • README-dev.txt — Original developer notes documenting the Windows 2000 SP4 build environment and runtime packaging.
  • TStore.NET/frmMain.vb — Visual Basic .NET upgraded form (`frmMain.vb`) preserving StoreTrainer functionality on modern .NET runtimes.
  • TStore.NET/TStore.vb — Visual Basic .NET core module ported from `TStore.bas`.
  • TStore.NET/SFile.vb — Visual Basic .NET file system module ported from `SFile.bas`.

Option Explicit


Private Sub Form_Load()
    SetFileName "untitled"
    SetFileFlag False, Me
End Sub



Private Sub Form_QueryUnload(Cancel As Integer, UnloadMode As Integer)
    Dim iMSG As VbMsgBoxResult
    
    ' When a StoreFile is launched, we must quickly close up
    If GetLaunchingSTF = True Then
        Cancel = False
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' A files is not being launched
    If GetFileFlag() = False Then
        iMSG = MsgBox("Are you sure you want to exit " & App.Title & "?", vbQuestion + vbYesNo)
        If iMSG = vbNo Then
            Cancel = True
        End If
        If iMSG = vbYes Then
            Cancel = False
        End If
    Else
        
        iMSG = MsgBox("Would you like to save your work before exiting?", vbQuestion + vbYesNoCancel, App.ProductName)
        If iMSG = vbYes Then
            ' File isn't saved yet.  Show a Save As dialog
            If LCase$(GetFileName()) = "untitled" Then
                Dim strSaveFile As String
                strSaveFile = DisplaySaveAs()
                If strSaveFile = "32755" Then
                    ' User clicked Cancel in the Save As dialog
                    Cancel = True
                    Exit Sub
                End If
                
                ' Write that filename to memory
                SetFileName (strSaveFile)
            End If
            
            ' Write data to disk
            SaveStoreFile Me, GetFileName()
            Cancel = False
        End If
        If iMSG = vbNo Then
            Cancel = False
        End If
        If iMSG = vbCancel Then
            ' Cancel.  No exit, No save.
            Cancel = True
        End If
    End If
End Sub


Private Sub chkLaunchGameFirst_Click()
    If chkLaunchGameFirst.value = True Then
        SetLaunchGameFirst True
        GoTo SetFlag
    End If
    If chkLaunchGameFirst.value = False Then
        SetLaunchGameFirst False
        GoTo SetFlag
    End If
SetFlag:
    SetFileFlag True, Me
End Sub

Private Sub chkTrainerLaunchesGame_Click()
    ' Turn on or off being able to locate a game if the trainer launches it
    Select Case chkTrainerLaunchesGame.value
        Case vbChecked
            SetTrainerLaunchesGame True
            Me.txtGamePath.Enabled = False
            Me.txtGameSwitch.Enabled = False
            Me.cmdBrowseGame.Enabled = False
            Me.mnuProjectBrowseGame.Enabled = False
            Me.mnuProjrectSwitchGame.Enabled = False
            Me.picXPShim2.Enabled = False
            Me.fraGameData.Enabled = False
            Me.lblGameSwitch.Enabled = False
            Me.txtGamePath.BackColor = vbButtonFace
            Me.txtGameSwitch.BackColor = vbButtonFace
            GoTo SetFlag
        Case vbUnchecked
            SetTrainerLaunchesGame False
            Me.txtGamePath.Enabled = True
            Me.txtGameSwitch.Enabled = True
            Me.cmdBrowseGame.Enabled = True
            Me.mnuProjectBrowseGame.Enabled = True
            Me.mnuProjrectSwitchGame.Enabled = True
            Me.picXPShim2.Enabled = True
            Me.fraGameData.Enabled = True
            Me.lblGameSwitch.Enabled = True
            Me.txtGamePath.BackColor = vbWindowBackground
            Me.txtGameSwitch.BackColor = vbWindowBackground
            GoTo SetFlag
    End Select
SetFlag:
    SetFileFlag True, Me
End Sub

Private Sub cmdBrowseGame_Click()
    On Error GoTo Trap
    Dim winInfo As osInfo
    With Me.cdgStoreFile
        .CancelError = True
        .Filter = "Executable Files (*.exe)|*.exe|All Files (*.*)|*.*"
        .DefaultExt = "exe"
        .DialogTitle = "Locate Game"
        .Flags = cdlOFNFileMustExist
        .InitDir = Environ("ProgramFiles") ' Default to %PROGRAM_FILES% since most games would be there (unlike SpecialFolder, this works on Win95/98)
        .ShowOpen
        Me.txtGamePath.Text = .FileName
        SetGamePath (.FileName)
    End With
    validateFile txtGamePath
    SetFileFlag True, Me
    Exit Sub
Trap:
    'User clicked cancel
    Exit Sub
End Sub

Private Sub cmdBrowseTrainer_Click()
    On Error GoTo Trap
    With Me.cdgStoreFile
        .CancelError = True
        .InitDir = FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_DOCUMENTS) '%MY_DOCUMENTS%
        .Filter = "Executable Files (*.exe)|*.exe|All Files (*.*)|*.*"
        .DefaultExt = "exe"
        .DialogTitle = "Locate Trainer"
        .Flags = cdlOFNFileMustExist
        .ShowOpen
        Me.txtTrainerPath.Text = .FileName
        SetTrainerPath (.FileName)
    End With
    validateFile txtTrainerPath
    SetFileFlag True, Me
    Exit Sub
Trap:
    'User clicked cancel
    Exit Sub
End Sub

Private Sub cmdLaunch_Click()
    doLaunch
End Sub

Private Function DisplaySaveAs() As String
    On Error GoTo Trapper:
    With Me.cdgStoreFile
        .CancelError = True
        .DialogTitle = "Save StoreFile"
        .Filter = "StoreFile (*.stf)|*.stf"
        .InitDir = GetStoreFileFolder()
        .DefaultExt = "stf"
        .ShowSave
        DisplaySaveAs = .FileName
    End With
    Exit Function
Trapper:
    If Err.Number = 32755 Then 'Cancel
        DisplaySaveAs = "32755"
        Exit Function
    End If
End Function


Private Sub mnuFileExit_Click()
    Unload Me
End Sub

Private Sub mnuFileNew_Click()
    createNewStoreFile
End Sub

Private Sub mnuFileOpen_Click()
    On Error GoTo Trapper
    With Me.cdgStoreFile
        .CancelError = True
        .DialogTitle = "Open StoreFile"
        .DefaultExt = "stf"
        .Filter = "StoreTrainer File (*.stf)|*.stf"
        .InitDir = GetStoreFileFolder()
        .Flags = cdlOFNFileMustExist
        .ShowOpen
        
        ' Reads STF data into StoreTrainer
        OpenStoreFile .FileName
        
        ' Brings StoreData into the form
        Me.chkLaunchGameFirst.value = GetLaunchGameFirst
        Me.chkTrainerLaunchesGame.value = GetTrainerLaunchesGame
        Me.txtGamePath.Text = GetGamePath
        Me.txtGameSwitch.Text = GetGameSwitch
        Me.txtTrainerPath.Text = GetTrainerPath
        Me.txtTrainerSwitch.Text = GetTrainerSwitch
        
        ' Sets our form name
        SetFileName .FileName
        SetFileFlag False, Me
    End With
    Exit Sub
Trapper:
    ' Assume CancelError
    Exit Sub
End Sub

Private Sub mnuFileSave_Click()
    ' Bring up Save As if needed
    Dim strFileName As String
    strFileName = GetFileName()
    If LCase$(strFileName = "untitled") Then
        mnuFileSaveAs_Click
    End If
    
    ' Write file to disk
    Dim iRet As Integer
    iRet = SaveStoreFile(Me, GetFileName)
    
    ' iRet is any error number the disk writing routine returns
    If iRet = 0 Then Exit Sub
    If iRet <> 0 Then
        Select Case iRet
            Case 32755: 'Cancel Button somewhere
                Exit Sub
            Case Else
                MsgBox "Error " & iRet
        End Select
    End If
End Sub

Private Sub mnuFileSaveAs_Click()
    ' Brings up a Save As dialog
    Dim strFile As String
    strFile = DisplaySaveAs()
    If strFile = "32755" Then
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' Continues with writing file to disk here
    SetFileName (strFile)
    mnuFileSave_Click
        
End Sub

Private Sub validateFile(txt As TextBox)
    If txt.Text = "" Then Exit Sub
    
    If DoesFileExist(txt.Text) = False Then
        txt.BackColor = vbRed
        MsgBox "The file " & Chr$(34) & txtGamePath.Text & Chr$(34) & " does not exist!", vbExclamation, App.Title
    Else
        txt.BackColor = vbWindowBackground
    End If
End Sub
Private Sub createNewStoreFile()
    Dim iMSG As VbMsgBoxResult
    If GetFileFlag = True Then
        ' Save first?
        iMSG = MsgBox("Would you like to save your work before creating a new StoreFile?", vbYesNoCancel + vbQuestion, App.Title)
        If iMSG = vbCancel Then Exit Sub
        If iMSG = vbYes Then
            mnuFileSave_Click
            GoTo CreateNewFile
        End If
        If iMSG = vbNo Then GoTo CreateNewFile
    End If
    
    If GetFileFlag = False Then
        iMSG = MsgBox("Close " & GetFileName(True) & " and create a new StoreFile?", vbYesNo + vbQuestion, App.Title)
        If iMSG = vbNo Then Exit Sub
        If iMSG = vbYes Then GoTo CreateNewFile
    End If
    
    ' Done the formalities.  Create our new StoreFile
CreateNewFile:
    NewStoreFile
    Me.chkLaunchGameFirst.value = GetLaunchGameFirst
    Me.chkTrainerLaunchesGame.value = GetTrainerLaunchesGame
    Me.txtGamePath.Text = GetGamePath
    Me.txtGameSwitch.Text = GetGameSwitch
    Me.txtTrainerPath.Text = GetTrainerPath
    Me.txtTrainerSwitch = GetTrainerSwitch
    SetFileFlag False, Me
End Sub

Private Sub doLaunch()
    Dim iLaunch As Integer
    iLaunch = Launch()
    If iLaunch <> 0 Then
        Select Case iLaunch
            Case 1 'File not saved
                MsgBox "Please save your work before launching the StoreFile!", vbExclamation, App.Title
                Exit Sub
            Case 2 ' Bad game path
                MsgBox "The game path you have doesn't exist!", vbExclamation, App.Title
                Exit Sub
            Case 3 'Bad trainer path
                MsgBox "The trainer path you have doesn't exist!", vbExclamation, App.Title
                Exit Sub
        End Select
    End If
End Sub

TStore.bas (Core Application Logic & Entrypoint)

[VB6 Core]

Core Visual Basic 6.0 module orchestrating initialization, profile loading, and Win32 execution flow.

Attribute VB_Name = "TStoreMod"
Option Explicit



' On Windows XP or later, turns on Visual Styles
Public Declare Function InitCommonControls Lib "comctl32.dll" () As Long

'Allows us to have a return code (use in place of an End statement)
Public Declare Sub ExitProcess Lib "kernel32" (ByVal uExitCode As Long)

Sub Main()
    ' Checks the command line to see if we have a file to operate on
    ' /e filename.stf to Edit a file
    ' /l filename.stf to Launch a file
    Dim intCmdReturn As Integer
    intCmdReturn = CheckCommandLine(Command$)
    
    ' Tells StoreTrainer that we want to turn on Visual Styles in Windows XP or later
    InitCommonControls
    
    ' Let's create TStore.INI if necessary
    If GetStoreTrainerDataFile = "" Then
        CreateStoreTrainerData
    End If
    
    ' Let's refresh the StoreTrainer Path if necessary
    ' This is primarily used for refreshing when switching from DEBUG to PRODUCTION
    Dim strCurPath As String
    strCurPath = IniGetValueString(GetStoreTrainerDataFile, "General", "Path", "PATH_NAME")
    If strCurPath <> App.Path Then
        Dim iMSG As VbMsgBoxResult
        iMSG = MsgBox("The " & App.ProductName & " configuration settings need to be updated.  Do that now?", vbYesNoCancel + vbQuestion, App.ProductName)
        If iMSG = vbCancel Then ExitProcess 4 'User Canceled updating TSTORE.INI
        If iMSG = vbYes Then
            IniWriteValueString GetStoreTrainerDataFile, "General", "Path", App.Path
        End If
    End If
        

    ' Let's make sure the StoreFile folder exists
    ' By default, it should be <MY_DOCUMENTS>\StoreFiles
    Dim strSTFFolder As String
    strSTFFolder = GetStoreFileFolder(True, True)
    If (strSTFFolder = "NO_FOLDER_CREATED") Then
        ' Error: folder does not exist, or wasn't created
        MsgBox App.ProductName & " requires that you create a StoreFile folder.  Now exiting!", vbCritical, App.ProductName
        
        ' Exit with a Code 1 ERROR_NO_STF_FOLDER
        ExitProcess 1
    End If
    ' Brings up the main screen
    frmMain.Show
End Sub

' This checks for a command line switch being passed in
' Returns an integer based on results:
' 0 - no command line switch found, load as normal
' 1 - File loaded for editing /e filename.stf
' 2 - File loaded for launching /l filename.stf
Public Function CheckCommandLine(Optional CommandLine As String = "") As Integer
    
End Function

Public Sub AboutStoreTrainer()
    MsgBox App.ProductName & " v" & App.Major & "." & App.Minor & "." & App.Revision & vbCrLf & "" & vbCrLf & "Copyright (C) 2024-2025 " & App.CompanyName, vbInformation + vbOKOnly, App.ProductName
End Sub

Public Sub CreateStoreTrainerData()
    ' First, let's create folders as necessary
    Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
    Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    If Not FSO.FolderExists(FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft") Then
        MkDir FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft"
    End If
    If Not FSO.FolderExists(FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer") Then
        MkDir FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer"
    End If
    
    ' Now, let's work on StoreTrainer data
    IniWriteValueString GetStoreTrainerDataDir & "\TStore.ini", "General", "Version", App.Major & "." & App.Minor & "." & App.Revision
    IniWriteValueString GetStoreTrainerDataDir & "\TStore.ini", "General", "Path", App.Path
End Sub

Public Function GetStoreTrainerDataDir() As String
    GetStoreTrainerDataDir = FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer"
End Function
Public Function GetStoreTrainerDataFile() As String
    If DoesFileExist(FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer\TStore.ini") Then
        GetStoreTrainerDataFile = FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer\TStore.ini"
    Else
        GetStoreTrainerDataFile = ""
    End If
End Function

SFile.bas (Flat-File & File System Operations)

[VB6 Win32 API]

Win32 file management and shell operations module for locating, copying, and launching game and trainer binaries.

Attribute VB_Name = "SFile"
Option Explicit
                 
' Holds our file data temporarily in memory
Private isFileDirty As Boolean
Private strFileName As String

Private StoreFileVersion As String 'YES, As String (file format limitation)

Private TrainerLaunchesGame As Boolean
Private LaunchGameFirst As Boolean

Private GamePath As String, GameSwitch As String
Private TrainerPath As String, TrainerSwitch As String

Private doLaunch As Boolean 'Fast Exit when launching a StoreFile

Public Function GetLaunchingSTF() As Boolean
    GetLaunchingSTF = doLaunch
End Function
Public Sub SetLaunchingSTF(boolDoLaunch As Boolean)
    doLaunch = boolDoLaunch
End Sub
' Returns the Release ID of the STF File Version.  Increment every time we need to update the file format
Public Function GetSTFVersionStr() As String
    GetSTFVersionStr = "1.0"
End Function

' Returns the same as above, but converted to a Long to make math comparison easy
Public Function GetSTFVersionLng() As Long
    GetSTFVersionLng = CLng(GetSTFVersionStr)
End Function

' New StoreFile (remember to work the form)
Public Sub NewStoreFile()
    SetLaunchGameFirst False
    SetTrainerLaunchesGame False
    SetGamePath ""
    SetGameSwitch ""
    SetTrainerPath ""
    SetTrainerSwitch ""
    SetFileName "untitled"
End Sub

' Some trainers expect the game to be launched first
Public Function GetLaunchGameFirst() As Boolean
    GetLaunchGameFirst = LaunchGameFirst
End Function
Public Sub SetLaunchGameFirst(boolLaunchGameFirst As Boolean)
    LaunchGameFirst = boolLaunchGameFirst
End Sub

Public Sub SetTrainerLaunchesGame(boolLaunchType As Boolean)
    TrainerLaunchesGame = boolLaunchType
End Sub
Public Function GetTrainerLaunchesGame() As Boolean
    GetTrainerLaunchesGame = TrainerLaunchesGame
End Function

Public Function GetGamePath() As String
    GetGamePath = GamePath
End Function
Public Sub SetGamePath(strGamePath As String)
    GamePath = strGamePath
End Sub
Public Function GetTrainerPath() As String
    GetTrainerPath = TrainerPath
End Function
Public Sub SetTrainerPath(strTrainerPath As String)
    TrainerPath = strTrainerPath
End Sub
Public Function GetGameSwitch() As String
    GetGameSwitch = GameSwitch
End Function
Public Sub SetGameSwitch(strGameSwitch As String)
    GameSwitch = strGameSwitch
End Sub
Public Function GetTrainerSwitch() As String
    GetTrainerSwitch = TrainerSwitch
End Function
Public Sub SetTrainerSwitch(strTrainerSwitch As String)
    TrainerSwitch = strTrainerSwitch
End Sub
' File Access Functions

' Tells StoreTrainer if the file is saved or not
Public Sub SetFileFlag(dirtyFlag As Boolean, frmName As Form)
    On Error GoTo ErrorTrap
    Dim errorType As String
    errorType = "Not Yet Set"
    If dirtyFlag = True Then
        errorType = "Dirty = true"
        isFileDirty = True
        frmName.Caption = GetFileName(True) & " * - " & App.ProductName
    ElseIf dirtyFlag = False Then
        errorType = "Dirty = false"
        isFileDirty = False
        errorType = errorType & " - Did Set Flag"
        frmName.Caption = GetFileName(True) & " - " & App.ProductName
        errorType = errorType & " - Did (not) Set Form Name"
    Else
        MsgBox "Improper Usage: setFileFlag() requires true or false!", vbExclamation + vbOKOnly, App.ProductName
        errorType = "Improper Usage"
    End If
    Exit Sub
ErrorTrap:
    MsgBox errorType & vbCrLf & Err.Number & ": " & Err.Description
End Sub

' Queries the Dirty state
Public Function GetFileFlag() As Boolean
    GetFileFlag = isFileDirty
End Function


' This writes StoreFile data to disk
Public Function SaveStoreFile(frmName As Form, strFileName As String) As Integer
    On Error GoTo ErrorTrapper
    ' Write StoreFile data to the disk
    
    ' General Info
    IniWriteValueString strFileName, "General", "STF.Version", GetSTFVersionStr
    
    
    ' Trainer Launches Game
    Dim strTrainerLaunchesGame As String
    If GetTrainerLaunchesGame() = True Then
        strTrainerLaunchesGame = "true"
    End If
    If GetTrainerLaunchesGame() = False Then
        strTrainerLaunchesGame = "false"
    End If
    IniWriteValueString strFileName, "Trainer", "TrainerLaunchesGame", strTrainerLaunchesGame
    
    ' Launch Game First
    Dim strLaunchGameFirst As String
    If GetLaunchGameFirst() = True Then
        strLaunchGameFirst = "true"
    End If
    If GetLaunchGameFirst() = False Then
        strLaunchGameFirst = "false"
    End If
    IniWriteValueString strFileName, "Game", "LaunchGameFirst", strLaunchGameFirst
    
    ' Write Game and Trainer info
    IniWriteValueString strFileName, "Game", "Path", GetGamePath
    IniWriteValueString strFileName, "Game", "Switch", GetGameSwitch
    
    IniWriteValueString strFileName, "Trainer", "Path", GetTrainerPath
    IniWriteValueString strFileName, "Trainer", "Switch", GetTrainerSwitch
    
    ' Unset the Dirty flag
    SetFileFlag False, frmName
    
    ' Reports no error on saving
    SaveStoreFile = 0
    Exit Function
    
    ' Error Trapping
ErrorTrapper: '
    
    SaveStoreFile = Err.Number
End Function

' Opens a StoreFile.  NOTE: this does NOT fill in the textboxes on a form
' Any return non-zero is an error
Public Function OpenStoreFile(strFilePath As String) As Integer
    Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
    Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    
    'Let's see if the file exists or not (return 53 (the same as VB6's File Not Found error) if it doesn't)
    If Not FSO.FileExists(strFilePath) Then
        OpenStoreFile = 53
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' File does exist.  Let's make sure it's a StoreFile this version of StoreTrainer understands
    Dim strSTFVersion As String
    strSTFVersion = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "General", "STF.Version", "0.0")
    Dim iSTFCompare As Integer
    iSTFCompare = CheckVersion(strSTFVersion, GetSTFVersionStr)
    
    ' The file being opened expects a newer version of StoreTrainer
    If iSTFCompare = 1 Then
        OpenStoreFile = 1
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' The file being opened expects an older version of StoreTrainer
    If iSTFCompare = -1 Then
        OpenStoreFile = 2
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' Now, let's load data into memory
    ' THIS WILL NOT LOAD DATA INTO A FORM
    
    ' Load Launch Data
    Dim strTrainerLaunchesGame As String
    strTrainerLaunchesGame = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "TrainerLaunchesGame", "false")
    
    If strTrainerLaunchesGame = "true" Then
        SetTrainerLaunchesGame True
    Else
        SetTrainerLaunchesGame False
    End If
    
    Dim strLaunchGameFirst As String
    strLaunchGameFirst = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "LaunchGameFirst", "false")
    If strLaunchGameFirst = "true" Then
        SetLaunchGameFirst True
    Else
        SetLaunchGameFirst False
    End If
    
    ' Get the Game and Trainer path and switches
    SetGamePath IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "Path", vbNullString)
    SetGameSwitch IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "Switch", vbNullString)
    
    SetTrainerPath IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "Path", vbNullString)
    SetTrainerSwitch IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "Switch", vbNullString)
    
    ' We're done. It is up to you to populate the form
    OpenStoreFile = 0
End Function

Public Sub SetFileName(strLocalFileName As String)
    strFileName = strLocalFileName
End Sub

Public Function GetFileName(Optional showFileNameOnly As Boolean) As String
    On Error GoTo cantReadRegistry
    ' Pull the filename from memory
    Dim strLocalFileName As String
    strLocalFileName = strFileName
    Dim boolHideExtensions As Boolean
    If showFileNameOnly = True Then
        ' Needed if the user wants to only show the filename without path
        Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
        Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
        ' Return the filename without a path
        ' First, we see if the user wants file extensions hidden or not (it's a user setting in Windows Explorer)
        ' Apparently this is hardened in Vista+ (see cantReadRegistry below)
        boolHideExtensions = CBool(RegGetValue$(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, "Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced", "HideFileExt"))
        If boolHideExtensions Then
            strLocalFileName = FSO.GetBaseName(strLocalFileName)
        Else
            strLocalFileName = FSO.GetFileName(strLocalFileName)
        End If
        
        ' Return that to the user
        GetFileName = strLocalFileName
        Exit Function
    End If
    ' Return the full filename
    GetFileName = strFileName
    Exit Function
cantReadRegistry:
    ' assume we don't have access to the Registry, we will NOT hide the extensions
    ' Seems to be an issue with newer versions of Windows (because VB6 doesn't understand Registry Security)
    boolHideExtensions = False
    Resume Next
End Function

Public Function Launch() As Integer
    ' Let's launch our StoreFile.  RULES:
    ' * File must NOT be dirty
    ' * Game and Trainer path MUST exist (unless of course, the trainer launches the game)
    ' * Returns an integer based on error type.  Anything non-zero means error
    
    ' Set up the FileSystem object
    Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
    Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    
    ' Is the file dirty?
    If GetFileFlag = True Or GetFileName = "untitled" Then
        Launch = 1 ' File isn't saved.  Return code 1
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' Look for the trainer
    If DoesFileExist(GetTrainerPath) = False Then
        Launch = 2 ' Trainer doesn't exist.  Return code 2
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' Look for the game (if it's NOT launched by the trainer)
    If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = False Then
        If DoesFileExist(GetGamePath) = False Then
            Launch = 3 ' Game doesn't exist.  Return code 3
            Exit Function
        End If
    End If
    
    ' Checked all our errors.  Let's launch files
    ' Let's build our file paths
    Dim strGameAndSwitch As String, strTrainerAndSwitch As String
    strGameAndSwitch = Chr$(34) & GetGamePath & Chr$(34)
    If GetGameSwitch <> "" Then
        strGameAndSwitch = strGameAndSwitch & " " & Chr$(34) & GetGameSwitch & Chr$(34)
    End If
    strTrainerAndSwitch = Chr$(34) & GetTrainerPath & Chr$(34)
    If GetTrainerSwitch <> "" Then
        strTrainerAndSwitch = strTrainerAndSwitch & " " & Chr$(34) & GetTrainerSwitch & Chr$(34)
    End If
    
    ' We are ready to launch.  Don't forget to get the ParentFolder property because some trainers (and games?) expect the working folder to be set
    
    ' Now to see what to launch
    If GetLaunchGameFirst = True Then
        
        ' Fall back, just in case
        If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = False Then
            ChDrive GetGamePath()
            ChDir GetGamePath()
            Shell strGameAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
            DoEvents
        End If
        ChDrive GetTrainerPath()
        ChDir GetTrainerPath()
        Shell strTrainerAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
        DoEvents
        Launch = 0
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' We just need to launch the trainer
    If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = True Then
        ChDrive GetTrainerPath()
        ChDir GetTrainerPath()
        Shell strTrainerAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
        Launch = 0
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' None of the options are selected.  Launch both
    ChDrive GetGamePath()
    ChDir GetGamePath()
    Shell strGameAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
    DoEvents
    ChDrive GetTrainerPath()
    ChDir GetTrainerPath()
    Shell strTrainerAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
    DoEvents
    Launch = 0
    Exit Function
    
End Function

INIFile.bas (Win32 kernel32 INI Configuration Parser)

[VB6 Win32 API]

Direct Win32 `GetPrivateProfileString` / `WritePrivateProfileString` (`kernel32.dll`) bindings for zero-database INI configuration persistence.

Attribute VB_Name = "INIFile"
Option Explicit

 'API DECLARATIONS
Declare Function GetPrivateProfileString Lib "kernel32" Alias _
                 "GetPrivateProfileStringA" (ByVal lpApplicationName _
                 As String, ByVal lpKeyName As Any, ByVal lpDefault _
                 As String, ByVal lpReturnedString As String, ByVal _
                 nSize As Long, ByVal lpFileName As String) As Long
Declare Function WritePrivateProfileString Lib "kernel32" Alias _
                 "WritePrivateProfileStringA" (ByVal lpApplicationName _
                 As String, ByVal lpKeyName As Any, ByVal lpString As Any, _
                 ByVal lpFileName As String) As Long

Public Function IniGetValueString(sINIFile As String, sSection As String, sKey _
                As String, sDefault As String) As String
    Dim sTemp As String * 256
    Dim nLength As Integer
    sTemp = Space$(256)
    nLength = GetPrivateProfileString(sSection, sKey, sDefault, sTemp, _
              255, sINIFile)
    IniGetValueString = Left$(sTemp, nLength)
End Function
Public Sub IniWriteValueString(sINIFile As String, sSection As String, sKey _
           As String, sValue As String)
    Dim n As Integer
    Dim sTemp As String
    sTemp = sValue
    'Replace any CR/LF characters with spaces
    For n = 1 To Len(sValue)
        If Mid$(sValue, n, 1) = vbCr Or Mid$(sValue, n, 1) = vbLf _
        Then Mid$(sValue, n) = " "
    Next n
    n = WritePrivateProfileString(sSection, sKey, sTemp, sINIFile)
End Sub

Registry.bas (Win32 advapi32 Registry Module)

[VB6 Win32 API]

Direct Win32 `RegOpenKeyEx` / `RegQueryValueEx` (`advapi32.dll`) bindings for reading game installation paths across 32-bit and 64-bit Windows.

Attribute VB_Name = "Registry"
Option Explicit

Type SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES
        nLength As Long
        lpSecurityDescriptor As Long
        bInheritHandle As Long
End Type

Public Declare Function RegCreateKeyEx& Lib "advapi32.dll" Alias "RegCreateKeyExA" (ByVal hKey&, ByVal lpSubKey$, ByVal Reserved&, ByVal lpClass$, ByVal dwOptions&, ByVal samDesired&, lpSecurityAttributes As SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES, phkResult&, lpdwDisposition&)
Public Declare Function RegSetValueEx& Lib "advapi32.dll" Alias "RegSetValueExA" (ByVal hKey&, ByVal lpszValueName$, ByVal dwRes&, ByVal dwType&, lpDataBuff As Any, ByVal nSize&)


Private Declare Function RegCloseKey& Lib "advapi32.dll" (ByVal hKey&)
Private Declare Function RegOpenKeyExA& Lib "advapi32.dll" (ByVal hKey&, ByVal lpszSubKey$, dwOptions&, ByVal samDesired&, lpHKey&)
Private Declare Function RegQueryValueExA& Lib "advapi32.dll" (ByVal hKey&, ByVal lpszValueName$, ByVal lpdwRes&, lpdwType&, ByVal lpDataBuff$, nSize&)
Private Declare Function RegQueryValueEx& Lib "advapi32.dll" Alias "RegQueryValueExA" (ByVal hKey&, ByVal lpszValueName$, ByVal lpdwRes&, lpdwType&, lpDataBuff&, nSize&)

Public Const HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT = &H80000000
Public Const HKEY_CURRENT_USER = &H80000001
Public Const HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE = &H80000002
Public Const HKEY_USERS = &H80000003

Public Const ERROR_SUCCESS = 0&
Public Const REG_SZ = 1&                          ' Unicode nul terminated string
Public Const REG_DWORD = 4&                       ' 32-bit number

Public Const KEY_QUERY_VALUE = &H1&
Public Const KEY_SET_VALUE = &H2&
Public Const KEY_CREATE_SUB_KEY = &H4&
Public Const KEY_ENUMERATE_SUB_KEYS = &H8&
Public Const KEY_NOTIFY = &H10&
Public Const KEY_CREATE_LINK = &H20&
Public Const READ_CONTROL = &H20000
Public Const WRITE_DAC = &H40000
Public Const WRITE_OWNER = &H80000
Public Const SYNCHRONIZE = &H100000
Public Const STANDARD_RIGHTS_REQUIRED = &HF0000
Public Const STANDARD_RIGHTS_READ = READ_CONTROL
Public Const STANDARD_RIGHTS_WRITE = READ_CONTROL
Public Const STANDARD_RIGHTS_EXECUTE = READ_CONTROL
Public Const KEY_READ = STANDARD_RIGHTS_READ Or KEY_QUERY_VALUE Or KEY_ENUMERATE_SUB_KEYS Or KEY_NOTIFY
Public Const KEY_WRITE = STANDARD_RIGHTS_WRITE Or KEY_SET_VALUE Or KEY_CREATE_SUB_KEY
Public Const KEY_EXECUTE = KEY_READ

Public Function RegGetValue$(MainKey&, SubKey$, value$)
   ' MainKey must be one of the Publicly declared HKEY constants.
   Dim sKeyType&       'to return the key type.  This function expects REG_SZ or REG_DWORD
   Dim ret&            'returned by registry functions, should be 0&
   Dim lpHKey&         'return handle to opened key
   Dim lpcbData&       'length of data in returned string
   Dim ReturnedString$ 'returned string value
   Dim ReturnedLong&   'returned long value
   If MainKey >= &H80000000 And MainKey <= &H80000006 Then
      ' Open key
      ret = RegOpenKeyExA(MainKey, SubKey, 0&, KEY_READ, lpHKey)
      If ret <> ERROR_SUCCESS Then
         RegGetValue = ""
         Exit Function     'No key open, so leave
      End If
      
      ' Set up buffer for data to be returned in.
      ' Adjust next value for larger buffers.
      lpcbData = 255
      ReturnedString = Space$(lpcbData)

      ' Read key
      ret& = RegQueryValueExA(lpHKey, value, ByVal 0&, sKeyType, ReturnedString, lpcbData)
      If ret <> ERROR_SUCCESS Then
         RegGetValue = ""   'Value probably doesn't exist
      Else
        If sKeyType = REG_DWORD Then
            ret = RegQueryValueEx(lpHKey, value, ByVal 0&, sKeyType, ReturnedLong, 4)
            If ret = ERROR_SUCCESS Then RegGetValue = CStr(ReturnedLong)
        Else
            RegGetValue = Left$(ReturnedString, lpcbData - 1)
        End If
    End If
      ' Always close opened keys.
      ret = RegCloseKey(lpHKey)
   End If
End Function

Public Sub RegSetValue(H_KEY&, RSubKey$, ValueName$, RegValue$)
    'H_KEY must be one of the Key Constants
    Dim lRtn&         'returned by registry functions, should be 0&
    Dim hKey&         'return handle to opened key
    Dim lpDisp&
    Dim Sec_Att As SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES
    Sec_Att.nLength = 12&
    Sec_Att.lpSecurityDescriptor = 0&
    Sec_Att.bInheritHandle = False
    If RegValue = "" Then RegValue = " "
    
        lRtn = RegCreateKeyEx(H_KEY, RSubKey, 0&, "", 0&, KEY_WRITE, Sec_Att, hKey, lpDisp)
        If lRtn <> 0 Then
            Exit Sub       'No key open, so leave
        End If
        lRtn = RegSetValueEx(hKey, ValueName, 0&, REG_SZ, ByVal RegValue, CLng(Len(RegValue) + 1))
        lRtn = RegCloseKey(hKey)
End Sub

SpecialFolder.bas (Win32 Shell Special Folders API)

[VB6 Win32 API]

Resolves `AppData`, `Program Files`, and user profile directories across Windows 95 through Windows 11.

Attribute VB_Name = "SpecialFolder"
Option Explicit


' Gives us access to Special Folders
Declare Function SHGetSpecialFolderLocation Lib "Shell32.dll" _
(ByVal hwndOwner As Long, ByVal nFolder As Long, pidl As ITEMIDLIST) As Long
Declare Function SHGetPathFromIDList Lib "Shell32.dll" Alias "SHGetPathFromIDListA" _
(ByVal pidl As Long, ByVal pszPath As String) As Long

Public Type SHITEMID
    cb As Long
    abID As Byte
End Type

Public Type ITEMIDLIST
    mkid As SHITEMID
End Type
Public Const MAX_PATH As Integer = 260

' List of folders
Public Enum SpecialFolderID
     CSIDL_DESKTOP = &H0 '// The Desktop - virtual folder
     CSIDL_APPDATA = &H1A '// Roaming App Data (anywhere on network)
     CSIDL_COMMONAPPDATA = &H23 '// Common App Data (probably do NOT have permission)
     CSIDL_LOCALAPPDATA = &H1C '// Same as App Data, but stays LOCAL to computer
     CSIDL_PROGRAMS = 2 '// Start Menu\Programs (DO NOT CONFUSE WITH THE PROGRAM FILES FOLDER!!)
     CSIDL_CONTROLS = 3 '// Control Panel - virtual folder
     CSIDL_PRINTERS = 4 '// Printers - virtual folder
     CSIDL_DOCUMENTS = 5 '// My Documents
     CSIDL_FAVORITES = 6 '// Favourites
     CSIDL_STARTUP = 7 '// Startup Folder
     CSIDL_RECENT = 8 '// Recent Documents
     CSIDL_SENDTO = 9 '// Send To Folder
     CSIDL_BITBUCKET = 10 '// Recycle Bin - virtual folder
     CSIDL_STARTMENU = 11 '// Start Menu
     CSIDL_DESKTOPFOLDER = 16 '// Desktop folder
     CSIDL_DRIVES = 17 '// My Computer - virtual folder
     CSIDL_NETWORK = 18 '// Network Neighbourhood - virtual folder
     CSIDL_NETHOOD = 19 '// NetHood Folder
     CSIDL_FONTS = 20 '// Fonts folder
     CSIDL_SHELLNEW = 21 '// ShellNew folder
End Enum

Public Function FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL As SpecialFolderID) As String
    Dim sPath As String
    Dim IDL As ITEMIDLIST
    '
    ' Retrieve info about system folders such as the "Recent Documents" folder.
    ' Info is stored in the IDL structure.
    '
    FGetSpecialFolder = ""
    If SHGetSpecialFolderLocation(GetForegroundWindow(), CSIDL, IDL) = 0 Then
        '
        ' Get the path from the ID list, and return the folder.
        '
        sPath = Space$(MAX_PATH)
        If SHGetPathFromIDList(ByVal IDL.mkid.cb, ByVal sPath) Then
            FGetSpecialFolder = Left$(sPath, InStr(sPath, vbNullChar) - 1) & ""
        End If
    End If
End Function


Public Function GetStoreFileFolder(Optional doCreateFolder As Boolean = False, Optional doPromptCreateFolder As Boolean = False) As String
    Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
    Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    If DoesFolderExist(iniGetValueString(getStoreTrainerDataFile, "Library", "Folder", vbNullString)) Then
        ' My Documents\StoreFiles exists.  Give it to the user
        GoTo ReturnFolder
    Else
        ' The folder does not exist
        If doCreateFolder Then
            ' The user wants to create the folder
            If doPromptCreateFolder Then
                ' The user needs a Yes/No
                Dim msgCreateFolder As VbMsgBoxResult
                msgCreateFolder = MsgBox("The StoreFile folder does not exist.  Create it?", vbYesNo + vbQuestion, App.ProductName)
                If (msgCreateFolder = vbYes) Then
                    GoTo CreateFolder
                Else
                    GoTo NoFolderCreated
                End If
            End If
        Else
            ' Folder wasn't created
            GoTo NoFolderCreated
        End If
    End If
    
    ' Creates the folder
CreateFolder:
    
    ' Create the StoreFiles folder
    On Error GoTo NoFolderCreatedShowError
    Dim strTStoreLibrary As String
    Dim winInfo As osInfo
    Dim strMyDocuments As String
    Dim errorLocation As Integer
    strMyDocuments = FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_DOCUMENTS)
    If DoesFolderExist(strMyDocuments & "\My StoreFiles") = False Then
        FSO.CreateFolder strMyDocuments & "\My StoreFiles"
    End If
    strTStoreLibrary = strMyDocuments & "\My StoreFiles"
    
    iniWriteValueString getStoreTrainerDataFile, "Library", "Folder", strTStoreLibrary
    MsgBox "StoreFile Library successfully created at: " & strTStoreLibrary, vbInformation, App.Title
    
    GoTo ReturnFolder
    
    ' Returns the folder path
ReturnFolder:
    GetStoreFileFolder = iniGetValueString(getStoreTrainerDataFile, "Library", "Folder", "NO_FOLDER_CREATED")
    Exit Function
    
NoFolderCreatedShowError:
    MsgBox Err.Number & " - " & Err.Description & vbCrLf & strMyDocuments
NoFolderCreated:
    
    ' Folder doesn't exist, user didn't create
    GetStoreFileFolder = "NO_FOLDER_CREATED"
                
End Function

' Does a folder exist?
Public Function DoesFolderExist(strFullPath As String) As Boolean
    Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
    Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    
    DoesFolderExist = FSO.FolderExists(strFullPath)
End Function

' Does a file exist?
Public Function DoesFileExist(strFullPath As String) As Boolean
    Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
    Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    
    DoesFileExist = FSO.FileExists(strFullPath)
End Function

OSVersionInfo.bas (Win32 GetVersionEx OS Detector)

[VB6 Win32 API]

Queries `GetVersionExA` (`OSVERSIONINFO`) to detect Windows 9x vs. Windows NT kernels at runtime.

Attribute VB_Name = "OSVersionInfo"
Option Explicit
' NOTE: in order for calls to GetVersionEx to function properly,
' you must include a manifest file with correct supportedOS entries
'
' Otherwise, calls will always return 6.2 at most on VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT

Private Declare Function GetVersionEx Lib "kernel32" Alias "GetVersionExA" _
    (lpVersionInformation As OSVERSIONINFO) As Long

Private Type OSVERSIONINFO
  OSVSize         As Long
  dwVerMajor      As Long
  dwVerMinor      As Long
  dwBuildNumber   As Long
  PlatformID      As Long
  szCSDVersion    As String * 128
End Type

Public Enum osArch
    VER_PLATFORM_WIN32s = 0 'Windows 3.x with Win32s Library
    VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_WINDOWS = 1 'Windows 9x
    VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT = 2 'Windows NT
End Enum
' Let's provide a public way to access Version Information
Public Type osInfo
    osArchitecture As osArch
    osVersionMajor As Long
    osVersionMinor As Long
    osVersionBuild As Long
    osServicePack As Long
End Type

Public Function GetWinVer() As osInfo
    Dim osv As OSVERSIONINFO
    osv.OSVSize = Len(osv)
    If GetVersionEx(osv) = 1 Then
        GetWinVer.osVersionMajor = osv.dwVerMajor
        GetWinVer.osVersionMinor = osv.dwVerMinor
        GetWinVer.osVersionBuild = osv.dwBuildNumber
        GetWinVer.osServicePack = -1 'Trap for no service pack (Windows 9x?)
        Select Case osv.PlatformID
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32s
                GetWinVer.osArchitecture = VER_PLATFORM_WIN32s
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT
                GetWinVer.osArchitecture = VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT
                
                ' Service Pack
                
                
                
                ' It's a pain in the rear to strip the number from the string, but here goes
                ' We're going from a String() - a Character Array - to a String to a Long
                Dim pos As Integer
                pos = InStr(osv.szCSDVersion, Chr$(0)) 'Get the string "Service Pack #" as an Array
                If pos Then
                    On Error GoTo NoSP 'Handle not having a Service Pack
                    Dim sSPName As String
                    sSPName = Left$(osv.szCSDVersion, pos - 1) 'Convert from a String() to a String
                    sSPName = Right$(sSPName, 1) 'Strip the Service Pack number from the string
                    Dim lSPNum As Long
                    lSPNum = CLng(sSPName) 'Convert the service pack number from a String to a Long
                    GetWinVer.osServicePack = lSPNum 'Offer it to the user
                    GoTo FinishNT 'We're done, if a Service Pack is installed
NoSP:
                    GetWinVer.osServicePack = 0 'No Service Pack installed (or we couldn't parse the Service Pack information)
                End If
FinishNT:
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_WINDOWS:
                GetWinVer.osArchitecture = VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_WINDOWS
        End Select

    End If

End Function

' Returns the version of Windows that the user is running
Public Function GetWindowsVersion() As String
    Dim osv As OSVERSIONINFO
    osv.OSVSize = Len(osv)

    If GetVersionEx(osv) = 1 Then
        Select Case osv.PlatformID
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32s
                GetWindowsVersion = "Win32s on Windows 3.1"
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT
                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows NT"

                Select Case osv.dwVerMajor
                    Case 3
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows NT 3.5"
                    Case 4
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows NT 4.0"
                    Case 5
                        Select Case osv.dwVerMinor
                            Case 0
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 2000"
                            Case 1
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows XP"
                            Case 2
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows Server 2003"
                        End Select
                    Case 6
                        Select Case osv.dwVerMinor
                            Case 0
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows Vista/Server 2008"
                            Case 1
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 7/Server 2008 R2"
                            Case 2
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 8/Server 2012"
                            Case 3
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 8.1/Server 2012 R2"
                        End Select
                    Case 10
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 10"
                End Select

            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_WINDOWS:
                Select Case osv.dwVerMinor
                    Case 0
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 95"
                    Case 90
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows Me"
                    Case Else
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 98"
                End Select
        End Select
    Else
        GetWindowsVersion = "Unable to identify your version of Windows."
    End If
End Function

DetectOSBits.bas (32-Bit vs. 64-Bit WOW64 Detection)

[VB6 Win32 API]

Dynamically probes `IsWow64Process` in `kernel32.dll` so 32-bit `TStore.exe` knows whether it is running on a 64-bit Windows OS.

Attribute VB_NAME = "DetectOSBits"
Option Explicit

Private Declare Function GetProcAddress Lib "kernel32" _
    (ByVal hModule As Long, ByVal lpProcName As String) As Long

Private Declare Function GetModuleHandle Lib "kernel32" _
    Alias "GetModuleHandleA" (ByVal lpModuleName As String) As Long

Private Declare Function GetCurrentProcess Lib "kernel32" () As Long

Private Declare Function IsWow64Process Lib "kernel32" _
    (ByVal hProc As Long, ByRef bWow64Process As Boolean) As Long

Public Function IsHost64Bit() As Boolean
    Dim handle As Long
    Dim is64Bit As Boolean

    ' Assume initially that this is not a WOW64 process
    is64Bit = False

    ' Then try to prove that wrong by attempting to load the
    ' IsWow64Process function dynamically
    handle = GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandle("kernel32"), "IsWow64Process")

    ' The function exists, so call it
    If handle <> 0 Then
        IsWow64Process GetCurrentProcess(), is64Bit
    End If

    ' Return the value
    IsHost64Bit = is64Bit
End Function

VersionCompare.bas (Binary File Version Comparator)

[VB6 Win32 API]

Uses `version.dll` (`GetFileVersionInfoA`) to inspect and compare executable version headers.

Attribute VB_Name = "VersionCompare"
Option Explicit
Public Function CompareFileVersion(sFileName1 As String, sFileName2 As String) As Integer

    '// Return values:
    '// -1 = File Version 2 is greater than File Version 1
    '//  0 = Versions are the same
    '//  1 = File version 1 is greater than File Version 2
    Dim iResult As Integer

    Dim sFileVersion1 As String
    Dim sFileVersion2 As String
    Dim arrFileVersion1() As String
    Dim arrFileVersion2() As String
    Dim lVersion1 As Long
    Dim lVersion2 As Long
    Dim fs As FileSystemObject

    '// Let's initialize our result with 0
    iResult = 0

    '// Use FileSystemObject to get the file version
    Set fs = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    sFileVersion1 = fs.GetFileVersion(sFileName1)
    sFileVersion2 = fs.GetFileVersion(sFileName2)

    '// Split the two supplied file versions by the "." character
    arrFileVersion1() = Split(sFileVersion1, ".")
    arrFileVersion2() = Split(sFileVersion2, ".")
    
    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 0 To UBound(arrFileVersion1())
        '// Convert the string to a number so we don't get false positive ("2">"19")
        lVersion1 = CLng(arrFileVersion1(i))
        lVersion2 = CLng(arrFileVersion2(i))
        If lVersion1 > lVersion2 Then
            iResult = 1
        ElseIf lVersion1 < lVersion2 Then
            iResult = -1
        End If

        'If we have found that the result is not > or <, no need to proceed
        If iResult <> 0 Then Exit For

    Next

    If UBound(arrFileVersion2) > UBound(arrFileVersion1) _
      And arrFileVersion2(UBound(arrFileVersion2)) <> 0 Then iResult = -1

    CompareFileVersion = iResult

End Function

Public Function CheckVersion(ByVal par1 As String, ByVal par2 As String) As Integer
    Dim arr1() As String
    Dim arr2() As String
    Dim looper As Integer
    Dim returnValue As Integer
    Dim val1 As Integer
    Dim val2 As Integer
    arr1 = Split(par1, ".")
    arr2 = Split(par2, ".")

    For looper = 0 To Max(UBound(arr1), UBound(arr2))
        val1 = 0
        val2 = 0
        If UBound(arr1) >= looper Then
            val1 = Val(arr1(looper))
        End If
        If UBound(arr2) >= looper Then
            val2 = Val(arr2(looper))
        End If

        If val1 > val2 Then
            returnValue = 1
            Exit For
        ElseIf val1 < val2 Then
            returnValue = -1
            Exit For
        Else
            ' same #, keep going
        End If
    Next
    CheckVersion = returnValue
End Function

Public Function Max(ByVal par1 As Integer, ByVal par2 As Integer) As Integer
    If par1 > par2 Then
        Max = par1
    Else
        Max = par2
    End If
End Function

README.txt (Original User Documentation)

[Documentation]

Original plaintext user documentation bundled with StoreTrainer.

RAGGIESOFT STORETRAINER
-----------------------

StoreTrainer is an easy way to remember the location of games and trainers (the common name for cheat programs).  StoreTrainer is an easy to use program, and when you first launch it, you will be taken directly to the StoreFile Editor.  The StoreFile is an easy-to-understand format, and you can get started with the Project menu which allows you to locate the Game and Trainer, as well as add command line switches to each program

SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS
-------------------

StoreTrainer should run on systems as old as Windows 95, as my goal is to be able to target the growing retro PC gaming market.  It is built using a Windows 2000 Professional machine and tested on Windows 2000 Professional as well as Windows 10 Professional, as I do not have access to a Windows 9x machine to test on.

VERSION HISTORY
---------------

Version 1.0
* Initial Release (rough around the edges)
 - Stores the location of games and their associated trainers

#Region "Upgrade Support "
	Private Shared m_vb6FormDefInstance As frmMain
	Private Shared m_InitializingDefInstance As Boolean
	Public Shared Property DefInstance() As frmMain
		Get
			If m_vb6FormDefInstance Is Nothing OrElse m_vb6FormDefInstance.IsDisposed Then
				m_InitializingDefInstance = True
				m_vb6FormDefInstance = New frmMain()
				m_InitializingDefInstance = False
			End If
			DefInstance = m_vb6FormDefInstance
		End Get
		Set
			m_vb6FormDefInstance = Value
		End Set
	End Property
#End Region 
	
	
	Private Sub frmMain_Load(ByVal eventSender As System.Object, ByVal eventArgs As System.EventArgs) Handles MyBase.Load
		SetFileName("untitled")
		SetFileFlag(False, Me)
		If DoesFileExist(VB6.GetPath & "\update.exe") = True Then
			Me.mnuHelpCheckForUpdate.Visible = True
		End If
		If DoesFileExist(VB6.GetPath & "\update.exe") = False Then
			Me.mnuHelpCheckForUpdate.Visible = False
		End If
	End Sub
	
	
	
	'UPGRADE_WARNING: Form event frmMain.QueryUnload has a new behavior. Click for more: 'ms-help://MS.VSCC.2003/commoner/redir/redirect.htm?keyword="vbup2065"'
	Private Sub frmMain_Closing(ByVal eventSender As System.Object, ByVal eventArgs As System.ComponentModel.CancelEventArgs) Handles MyBase.Closing
		Dim Cancel As Short = eventArgs.Cancel
		Dim iMSG As MsgBoxResult
		
		' When a StoreFile is launched, we must quickly close up
		If GetLaunchingSTF = True Then
			Cancel = False
			GoTo EventExitSub
		End If
		
		' A files is not being launched
		Dim strSaveFile As String
		If GetFileFlag() = False Then
			iMSG = MsgBox("Are you sure you want to exit " & System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.GetName.Name & "?", MsgBoxStyle.Question + MsgBoxStyle.YesNo)
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.No Then
				Cancel = True
			End If
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Yes Then
				Cancel = False
			End If
		Else
			
			iMSG = MsgBox("Would you like to save your work before exiting?", MsgBoxStyle.Question + MsgBoxStyle.YesNoCancel, System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName)
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Yes Then
				' File isn't saved yet.  Show a Save As dialog
				If LCase(GetFileName()) = "untitled" Then
					strSaveFile = DisplaySaveAs()
					If strSaveFile = "32755" Then
						' User clicked Cancel in the Save As dialog
						Cancel = True
						GoTo EventExitSub
					End If
					
					' Write that filename to memory
					SetFileName((strSaveFile))
				End If
				
				' Write data to disk
				SaveStoreFile(Me, GetFileName())
				Cancel = False
			End If
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.No Then
				Cancel = False
			End If
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Cancel Then
				' Cancel.  No exit, No save.
				Cancel = True
			End If
		End If
EventExitSub: 
		eventArgs.Cancel = Cancel
	End Sub
	
	
	'UPGRADE_WARNING: Event chkLaunchGameFirst.CheckStateChanged may fire when form is initialized. Click for more: 'ms-help://MS.VSCC.2003/commoner/redir/redirect.htm?keyword="vbup2075"'
	Private Sub chkLaunchGameFirst_CheckStateChanged(ByVal eventSender As System.Object, ByVal eventArgs As System.EventArgs) Handles chkLaunchGameFirst.CheckStateChanged
		If chkLaunchGameFirst.CheckState = True Then
			SetLaunchGameFirst(True)
			GoTo SetFlag
		End If
		If chkLaunchGameFirst.CheckState = False Then
			SetLaunchGameFirst(False)
			GoTo SetFlag
		End If
SetFlag: 
		SetFileFlag(True, Me)
	End Sub
	
	'UPGRADE_WARNING: Event chkTrainerLaunchesGame.CheckStateChanged may fire when form is initialized. Click for more: 'ms-help://MS.VSCC.2003/commoner/redir/redirect.htm?keyword="vbup2075"'
	Private Sub chkTrainerLaunchesGame_CheckStateChanged(ByVal eventSender As System.Object, ByVal eventArgs As System.EventArgs) Handles chkTrainerLaunchesGame.CheckStateChanged
		' Turn on or off being able to locate a game if the trainer launches it
		Select Case chkTrainerLaunchesGame.CheckState
			Case System.Windows.Forms.CheckState.Checked
				SetTrainerLaunchesGame(True)
				Me.txtGamePath.Enabled = False
				Me.txtGameSwitch.Enabled = False
				Me.cmdBrowseGame.Enabled = False
				Me.mnuProjectBrowseGame.Enabled = False
				Me.mnuProjrectSwitchGame.Enabled = False
				Me.picXPShim2.Enabled = False
				Me.fraGameData.Enabled = False
				Me.lblGameSwitch.Enabled = False
				Me.txtGamePath.BackColor = System.Drawing.SystemColors.Control
				Me.txtGameSwitch.BackColor = System.Drawing.SystemColors.Control
				GoTo SetFlag
			Case System.Windows.Forms.CheckState.Unchecked
				SetTrainerLaunchesGame(False)
				Me.txtGamePath.Enabled = True
				Me.txtGameSwitch.Enabled = True
				Me.cmdBrowseGame.Enabled = True
				Me.mnuProjectBrowseGame.Enabled = True
				Me.mnuProjrectSwitchGame.Enabled = True

		' Bring up Save As if needed
		Dim strFileName As String
		strFileName = GetFileName()
		If CBool(LCase(CStr(strFileName = "untitled"))) Then
			mnuFileSaveAs_Click(mnuFileSaveAs, New System.EventArgs())
		End If
		
		' Write file to disk
		Dim iRet As Short
		iRet = SaveStoreFile(Me, GetFileName)
		
		' iRet is any error number the disk writing routine returns
		If iRet = 0 Then Exit Sub
		If iRet <> 0 Then
			Select Case iRet
				Case 32755 'Cancel Button somewhere
					Exit Sub
				Case Else
					MsgBox("Error " & iRet)
			End Select
		End If
	End Sub

	Private Sub validateFile(ByRef txt As System.Windows.Forms.TextBox)
		If txt.Text = "" Then Exit Sub
		
		If DoesFileExist((txt.Text)) = False Then
			txt.BackColor = System.Drawing.Color.Red
			MsgBox("The file " & Chr(34) & txtGamePath.Text & Chr(34) & " does not exist!", MsgBoxStyle.Exclamation, System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.GetName.Name)
		Else
			txt.BackColor = System.Drawing.SystemColors.Window
		End If
	End Sub
	Private Sub createNewStoreFile()
		Dim iMSG As MsgBoxResult
		If GetFileFlag = True Then
			' Save first?
			iMSG = MsgBox("Would you like to save your work before creating a new StoreFile?", MsgBoxStyle.YesNoCancel + MsgBoxStyle.Question, System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.GetName.Name)
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Cancel Then Exit Sub
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Yes Then
				mnuFileSave_Click(mnuFileSave, New System.EventArgs())
				GoTo CreateNewFile
			End If
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.No Then GoTo CreateNewFile
		End If
		
		If GetFileFlag = False Then
			iMSG = MsgBox("Close " & GetFileName(True) & " and create a new StoreFile?", MsgBoxStyle.YesNo + MsgBoxStyle.Question, System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.GetName.Name)
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.No Then Exit Sub
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Yes Then GoTo CreateNewFile
		End If
		
		' Done the formalities.  Create our new StoreFile
CreateNewFile: 
		NewStoreFile()
		Me.chkLaunchGameFirst.CheckState = GetLaunchGameFirst
		Me.chkTrainerLaunchesGame.CheckState = GetTrainerLaunchesGame
		Me.txtGamePath.Text = GetGamePath
		Me.txtGameSwitch.Text = GetGameSwitch
		Me.txtTrainerPath.Text = GetTrainerPath
		Me.txtTrainerSwitch.Text = GetTrainerSwitch
		SetFileFlag(False, Me)
	End Sub
	
	Private Sub doLaunch()
		Dim iLaunch As Short
		iLaunch = Launch()
		If iLaunch <> 0 Then
			Select Case iLaunch
				Case 1 'File not saved
					MsgBox("Please save your work before launching the StoreFile!", MsgBoxStyle.Exclamation, System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.GetName.Name)
					Exit Sub
				Case 2 ' Bad game path
					MsgBox("The game path you have doesn't exist!", MsgBoxStyle.Exclamation, System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.GetName.Name)
					Exit Sub
				Case 3 'Bad trainer path
					MsgBox("The trainer path you have doesn't exist!", MsgBoxStyle.Exclamation, System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.GetName.Name)
					Exit Sub
			End Select
		End If
	End Sub
End Class

TStore.NET/TStore.vb (VB.NET Core Module)

[.NET Port]

Visual Basic .NET core module ported from `TStore.bas`.

Option Strict Off
Option Explicit On
Imports VB = Microsoft.VisualBasic
Module TStoreMod
	
	
	
	' On Windows XP or later, turns on Visual Styles
	Public Declare Function InitCommonControls Lib "comctl32.dll" () As Integer
	
	'Allows us to have a return code (use in place of an End statement)
	Public Declare Sub ExitProcess Lib "kernel32" (ByVal uExitCode As Integer)
	
	'UPGRADE_WARNING: Application will terminate when Sub Main() finishes. Click for more: 'ms-help://MS.VSCC.2003/commoner/redir/redirect.htm?keyword="vbup1047"'
	Public Sub Main()
		' Checks the command line to see if we have a file to operate on
		' /e filename.stf to Edit a file
		' /l filename.stf to Launch a file
		Dim intCmdReturn As Short
		intCmdReturn = CheckCommandLine(VB.Command())
		
		' Tells StoreTrainer that we want to turn on Visual Styles in Windows XP or later
		InitCommonControls()
		
		' Let's create TStore.INI if necessary
		If GetStoreTrainerDataFile = "" Then
			CreateStoreTrainerData()
		End If
		
		' Let's refresh the StoreTrainer Path if necessary
		' This is primarily used for refreshing when switching from DEBUG to PRODUCTION
		Dim strCurPath As String
		strCurPath = IniGetValueString(GetStoreTrainerDataFile, "General", "Path", "PATH_NAME")
		Dim iMSG As MsgBoxResult
		If strCurPath <> VB6.GetPath Then
			iMSG = MsgBox("The " & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName & " configuration settings need to be updated.  Do that now?", MsgBoxStyle.YesNoCancel + MsgBoxStyle.Question, System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName)
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Cancel Then ExitProcess(4) 'User Canceled updating TSTORE.INI
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Yes Then
				IniWriteValueString(GetStoreTrainerDataFile, "General", "Path", VB6.GetPath)
			End If
		End If
		
		
		' Let's make sure the StoreFile folder exists
		' By default, it should be <MY_DOCUMENTS>\StoreFiles
		Dim strSTFFolder As String
		strSTFFolder = GetStoreFileFolder(True, True)
		If (strSTFFolder = "NO_FOLDER_CREATED") Then
			' Error: folder does not exist, or wasn't created
			MsgBox(System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName & " requires that you create a StoreFile folder.  Now exiting!", MsgBoxStyle.Critical, System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName)
			
			' Exit with a Code 1 ERROR_NO_STF_FOLDER
			ExitProcess(1)
		End If
		' Brings up the main screen
		frmMain.DefInstance.Show()
	End Sub
	
	' This checks for a command line switch being passed in
	' Returns an integer based on results:
	' 0 - no command line switch found, load as normal
	' 1 - File loaded for editing /e filename.stf
	' 2 - File loaded for launching /l filename.stf
	Public Function CheckCommandLine(Optional ByRef CommandLine As String = "") As Short
		
	End Function
	
	Public Sub AboutStoreTrainer()
		'UPGRADE_ISSUE: App property App.Revision was not upgraded. Click for more: 'ms-help://MS.VSCC.2003/commoner/redir/redirect.htm?keyword="vbup2069"'
		MsgBox(System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName & " v" & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).FileMajorPart & "." & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).FileMinorPart & "." & App.Revision & vbCrLf & "" & vbCrLf & "Copyright (C) 2018 - 2021 " & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).CompanyName, MsgBoxStyle.Information + MsgBoxStyle.OKOnly, System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName)
	End Sub
	
	Public Sub CreateStoreTrainerData()
		' First, let's create folders as necessary
		Dim FSO As IWshRuntimeLibrary.FileSystemObject
		FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
		If Not FSO.FolderExists(FGetSpecialFolder(SpecialFolder.SpecialFolderID.CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft") Then
			MkDir(FGetSpecialFolder(SpecialFolder.SpecialFolderID.CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft")
		End If
		If Not FSO.FolderExists(FGetSpecialFolder(SpecialFolder.SpecialFolderID.CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer") Then
			MkDir(FGetSpecialFolder(SpecialFolder.SpecialFolderID.CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer")
		End If
		
		' Now, let's work on StoreTrainer data
		'UPGRADE_ISSUE: App property App.Revision was not upgraded. Click for more: 'ms-help://MS.VSCC.2003/commoner/redir/redirect.htm?keyword="vbup2069"'
		IniWriteValueString(GetStoreTrainerDataDir & "\TStore.ini", "General", "Version", System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).FileMajorPart & "." & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).FileMinorPart & "." & App.Revision)
		IniWriteValueString(GetStoreTrainerDataDir & "\TStore.ini", "General", "Path", VB6.GetPath)
	End Sub
	
	Public Function GetStoreTrainerDataDir() As String
		GetStoreTrainerDataDir = FGetSpecialFolder(SpecialFolder.SpecialFolderID.CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer"
	End Function
	Public Function GetStoreTrainerDataFile() As String
		If DoesFileExist(FGetSpecialFolder(SpecialFolder.SpecialFolderID.CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer\TStore.ini") Then
			GetStoreTrainerDataFile = FGetSpecialFolder(SpecialFolder.SpecialFolderID.CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer\TStore.ini"
		Else
			GetStoreTrainerDataFile = ""
		End If
	End Function
End Module

[.NET Port]

Visual Basic .NET file system module ported from `SFile.bas`.

Option Strict Off
Option Explicit On
Module SFile
	
	' Holds our file data temporarily in memory
	Private isFileDirty As Boolean
	Private strFileName As String
	
	Private StoreFileVersion As String 'YES, As String (file format limitation)
	
	Private TrainerLaunchesGame As Boolean
	Private LaunchGameFirst As Boolean
	
	Private GamePath, GameSwitch As String
	Private TrainerPath, TrainerSwitch As String
	
	Private doLaunch As Boolean 'Fast Exit when launching a StoreFile
	
	Public Function GetLaunchingSTF() As Boolean

	End Function
	Public Sub SetLaunchingSTF(ByRef boolDoLaunch As Boolean)
		doLaunch = boolDoLaunch
	End Sub
	' Returns the Release ID of the STF File Version.  Increment every time we need to update the file format
	Public Function GetSTFVersionStr() As String
		GetSTFVersionStr = "1.0"
	End Function
	
	' Returns the same as above, but converted to a Long to make math comparison easy
	Public Function GetSTFVersionLng() As Integer
		GetSTFVersionLng = CInt(GetSTFVersionStr)
	End Function
	
	' New StoreFile (remember to work the form)
	Public Sub NewStoreFile()
		SetLaunchGameFirst(False)
		SetTrainerLaunchesGame(False)
		SetGamePath("")
		SetGameSwitch("")
		SetTrainerPath("")
		SetTrainerSwitch("")
		SetFileName("untitled")
	End Sub
	
	' Some trainers expect the game to be launched first
	Public Function GetLaunchGameFirst() As Boolean
		GetLaunchGameFirst = LaunchGameFirst
	End Function
	Public Sub SetLaunchGameFirst(ByRef boolLaunchGameFirst As Boolean)
		LaunchGameFirst = boolLaunchGameFirst
	End Sub
	
	Public Sub SetTrainerLaunchesGame(ByRef boolLaunchType As Boolean)
		TrainerLaunchesGame = boolLaunchType
	End Sub
	Public Function GetTrainerLaunchesGame() As Boolean
		GetTrainerLaunchesGame = TrainerLaunchesGame
	End Function
	
	Public Function GetGamePath() As String
		GetGamePath = GamePath
	End Function
	Public Sub SetGamePath(ByRef strGamePath As String)
		GamePath = strGamePath
	End Sub
	Public Function GetTrainerPath() As String
		GetTrainerPath = TrainerPath
	End Function
	Public Sub SetTrainerPath(ByRef strTrainerPath As String)
		TrainerPath = strTrainerPath
	End Sub
	Public Function GetGameSwitch() As String
		GetGameSwitch = GameSwitch
	End Function
	Public Sub SetGameSwitch(ByRef strGameSwitch As String)
		GameSwitch = strGameSwitch
	End Sub
	Public Function GetTrainerSwitch() As String
		GetTrainerSwitch = TrainerSwitch
	End Function
	Public Sub SetTrainerSwitch(ByRef strTrainerSwitch As String)
		TrainerSwitch = strTrainerSwitch
	End Sub
	' File Access Functions
	
	' Tells StoreTrainer if the file is saved or not
	Public Sub SetFileFlag(ByRef dirtyFlag As Boolean, ByRef frmName As System.Windows.Forms.Form)
		On Error GoTo ErrorTrap
		Dim errorType As String
		errorType = "Not Yet Set"
		If dirtyFlag = True Then
			errorType = "Dirty = true"
			isFileDirty = True
			frmName.Text = GetFileName(True) & " * - " & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName
		ElseIf dirtyFlag = False Then 
			errorType = "Dirty = false"
			isFileDirty = False
			errorType = errorType & " - Did Set Flag"
			frmName.Text = GetFileName(True) & " - " & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName
			errorType = errorType & " - Did (not) Set Form Name"
		Else
			MsgBox("Improper Usage: setFileFlag() requires true or false!", MsgBoxStyle.Exclamation + MsgBoxStyle.OKOnly, System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName)
			errorType = "Improper Usage"
		End If
		Exit Sub
ErrorTrap: 
		MsgBox(errorType & vbCrLf & Err.Number & ": " & Err.Description)
	End Sub
	
	' Queries the Dirty state
	Public Function GetFileFlag() As Boolean
		GetFileFlag = isFileDirty
	End Function
	
	
	' This writes StoreFile data to disk
	Public Function SaveStoreFile(ByRef frmName As System.Windows.Forms.Form, ByRef strFileName As String) As Short
		On Error GoTo ErrorTrapper
		' Write StoreFile data to the disk
		
		' General Info
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "General", "STF.Version", GetSTFVersionStr)
		
		
		' Trainer Launches Game
		Dim strTrainerLaunchesGame As String
		If GetTrainerLaunchesGame() = True Then
			strTrainerLaunchesGame = "true"
		End If
		If GetTrainerLaunchesGame() = False Then
			strTrainerLaunchesGame = "false"
		End If
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Trainer", "TrainerLaunchesGame", strTrainerLaunchesGame)
		
		' Launch Game First
		Dim strLaunchGameFirst As String
		If GetLaunchGameFirst() = True Then
			strLaunchGameFirst = "true"
		End If
		If GetLaunchGameFirst() = False Then
			strLaunchGameFirst = "false"
		End If
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Game", "LaunchGameFirst", strLaunchGameFirst)
		
		' Write Game and Trainer info
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Game", "Path", GetGamePath)
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Game", "Switch", GetGameSwitch)
		
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Trainer", "Path", GetTrainerPath)
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Trainer", "Switch", GetTrainerSwitch)
		
		' Unset the Dirty flag
		SetFileFlag(False, frmName)
		
		' Reports no error on saving
		SaveStoreFile = 0
		Exit Function
		
		' Error Trapping
ErrorTrapper: '
		
		SaveStoreFile = Err.Number
	End Function
	
	' Opens a StoreFile.  NOTE: this does NOT fill in the textboxes on a form
	' Any return non-zero is an error
	Public Function OpenStoreFile(ByRef strFilePath As String) As Short
		Dim FSO As IWshRuntimeLibrary.FileSystemObject
		FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
		
		'Let's see if the file exists or not (return 53 (the same as VB6's File Not Found error) if it doesn't)
		If Not FSO.FileExists(strFilePath) Then
			OpenStoreFile = 53
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' File does exist.  Let's make sure it's a StoreFile this version of StoreTrainer understands
		Dim strSTFVersion As String
		strSTFVersion = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "General", "STF.Version", "0.0")
		Dim iSTFCompare As Short
		iSTFCompare = CheckVersion(strSTFVersion, GetSTFVersionStr)
		
		' The file being opened expects a newer version of StoreTrainer
		If iSTFCompare = 1 Then
			OpenStoreFile = 1
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' The file being opened expects an older version of StoreTrainer
		If iSTFCompare = -1 Then
			OpenStoreFile = 2
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' Now, let's load data into memory
		' THIS WILL NOT LOAD DATA INTO A FORM
		
		' Load Launch Data
		Dim strTrainerLaunchesGame As String
		strTrainerLaunchesGame = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "TrainerLaunchesGame", "false")
		
		If strTrainerLaunchesGame = "true" Then
			SetTrainerLaunchesGame(True)
		Else
			SetTrainerLaunchesGame(False)
		End If
		
		Dim strLaunchGameFirst As String
		strLaunchGameFirst = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "LaunchGameFirst", "false")
		If strLaunchGameFirst = "true" Then
			SetLaunchGameFirst(True)
		Else
			SetLaunchGameFirst(False)
		End If
		
		' Get the Game and Trainer path and switches
		SetGamePath(IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "Path", vbNullString))
		SetGameSwitch(IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "Switch", vbNullString))
		
		SetTrainerPath(IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "Path", vbNullString))
		SetTrainerSwitch(IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "Switch", vbNullString))
		
		' We're done. It is up to you to populate the form
		OpenStoreFile = 0
	End Function
	
	Public Sub SetFileName(ByRef strLocalFileName As String)
		strFileName = strLocalFileName
	End Sub
	
	Public Function GetFileName(Optional ByRef showFileNameOnly As Boolean = False) As String
		On Error GoTo cantReadRegistry
		' Pull the filename from memory
		Dim strLocalFileName As String
		strLocalFileName = strFileName
		Dim boolHideExtensions As Boolean
		Dim FSO As IWshRuntimeLibrary.FileSystemObject
		If showFileNameOnly = True Then
			' Needed if the user wants to only show the filename without path
			FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
			' Return the filename without a path
			' First, we see if the user wants file extensions hidden or not (it's a user setting in Windows Explorer)
			' Apparently this is hardened in Vista+ (see cantReadRegistry below)
			boolHideExtensions = CBool(RegGetValue(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, "Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced", "HideFileExt"))
			If boolHideExtensions Then
				strLocalFileName = FSO.GetBaseName(strLocalFileName)
			Else
				strLocalFileName = FSO.GetFileName(strLocalFileName)
			End If
			
			' Return that to the user
			GetFileName = strLocalFileName
			Exit Function
		End If
		' Return the full filename
		GetFileName = strFileName
		Exit Function
cantReadRegistry: 
		' assume we don't have access to the Registry, we will NOT hide the extensions
		' Seems to be an issue with newer versions of Windows (because VB6 doesn't understand Registry Security)
		boolHideExtensions = False
		Resume Next
	End Function
	
	Public Function Launch() As Short
		' Let's launch our StoreFile.  RULES:
		' * File must NOT be dirty
		' * Game and Trainer path MUST exist (unless of course, the trainer launches the game)
		' * Returns an integer based on error type.  Anything non-zero means error
		
		' Set up the FileSystem object
		Dim FSO As IWshRuntimeLibrary.FileSystemObject
		FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
		
		' Is the file dirty?
		If GetFileFlag = True Or GetFileName = "untitled" Then
			Launch = 1 ' File isn't saved.  Return code 1
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' Look for the trainer
		If DoesFileExist(GetTrainerPath) = False Then
			Launch = 2 ' Trainer doesn't exist.  Return code 2
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' Look for the game (if it's NOT launched by the trainer)
		If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = False Then
			If DoesFileExist(GetGamePath) = False Then
				Launch = 3 ' Game doesn't exist.  Return code 3
				Exit Function
			End If
		End If
		
		' Checked all our errors.  Let's launch files
		' Let's build our file paths
		Dim strGameAndSwitch, strTrainerAndSwitch As String
		strGameAndSwitch = Chr(34) & GetGamePath & Chr(34)
		If GetGameSwitch <> "" Then
			strGameAndSwitch = strGameAndSwitch & " " & Chr(34) & GetGameSwitch & Chr(34)
		End If
		strTrainerAndSwitch = Chr(34) & GetTrainerPath & Chr(34)
		If GetTrainerSwitch <> "" Then
			strTrainerAndSwitch = strTrainerAndSwitch & " " & Chr(34) & GetTrainerSwitch & Chr(34)
		End If
		
		' We are ready to launch.  Don't forget to get the ParentFolder property because some trainers (and games?) expect the working folder to be set
		
		' Now to see what to launch
		If GetLaunchGameFirst = True Then
			
			' Fall back, just in case
			If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = False Then
				ChDrive(GetGamePath())
				ChDir(GetGamePath())
				Shell(strGameAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
				System.Windows.Forms.Application.DoEvents()
			End If
			ChDrive(GetTrainerPath())
			ChDir(GetTrainerPath())
			Shell(strTrainerAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
			System.Windows.Forms.Application.DoEvents()
			Launch = 0
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' We just need to launch the trainer
		If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = True Then
			ChDrive(GetTrainerPath())
			ChDir(GetTrainerPath())
			Shell(strTrainerAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
			Launch = 0
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' None of the options are selected.  Launch both
		ChDrive(GetGamePath())
		ChDir(GetGamePath())
		Shell(strGameAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
		System.Windows.Forms.Application.DoEvents()
		ChDrive(GetTrainerPath())
		ChDir(GetTrainerPath())
		Shell(strTrainerAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
		System.Windows.Forms.Application.DoEvents()
		Launch = 0
		Exit Function
		
	End Function
End Module
